title: Review Space discovery signals with explicit private permission
detail: Space editors explicitly enable ninety-day discovery_coaching permission stored in separate service-role-only discovery_consent, never public preferences or coach_profile. On-demand review resolves uncached current ownership or direct active editor/admin membership and consent before aggregate reads (staff preview and inferred network roles do not grant consent authority) and rechecks both after IO, discarding revoked or changed grants. Existing profile-view buckets and CTA events remain coarse limited observations, not unique visitors or attributed conversions. Owner UI shows source, counting unit, period, freshness, coverage, questions and measurement limits, plus expiry/revoke and unavailable states. Google Search Console and Bing are explicitly not connected. No scheduled refresh, provider writes, content generation or publication. Migration25100 remains unapplied. The release owner independently executed its exact SQL in a disposable database and all fourteen assertions passed (SHA2566b783385a473376dc4e348f230b0aea49fc353625f99e1fbdec1bfeddbab12c8). Full-schema DB CI and production apply/acceptance remain required before UI rollout. LIVE-1335 remains open for provider connectors and full discovery scope.

verify.evidence: 128 focused tests across eleven suites pass, including actual uncached membership reads under an adversarial sticky request cache, permission loss during aggregate IO, reauthorization before grant persistence, consent revocation and direct-editor page isolation. Bounded actual-source inert IO probe, scoped lint and fourteen root-run disposable SQL assertions pass. No production database/provider or authenticated UI acceptance is claimed.
